fuel-test-valve.summary: The diagnostic valve connects to the fuel rail through an open branch. A spring-returned pin carries a sealing washer away from its seat when depressed; the protective cap is removed from the isolated opening study.
fuel-test-valve.limits: The isolated motion is not integrated into viewer controls. The sampled 0–0.12 mm travel, spring geometry, thread dimensions and seal gaps are provisional. A 0.01 mm static-seal radial clearance remains unresolved; geometric connectivity does not establish leakage, pressure sealing or safe servicing.

steps.title: Connect to the rail
steps.text: The valve body meets the existing rail branch. The checked passage remains open into the cartridge without adding a second rail fitting.

steps.title: Distinguish cap protection from the working valve
steps.text: The cap and its illustrative seal are present in the installed state and excluded from the isolated uncapped states. Gauge attachment and a servicing procedure are not modeled.

steps.title: Unseat the moving washer
steps.text: The pin and seating washer move together, opening the intended route across the annular seat. The same diagnostic route is blocked in the closed-state control.

steps.title: Shorten the return spring
steps.text: The modeled spring shortens with the pin over four sampled open positions. This checks geometric clearance only; no actual spring rate, preload or stroke is established.

steps.title: Keep bypass sealing unresolved
steps.text: The separate static seal is intended to close the route around the cartridge, but its current clearance is not a compressed production seal. A clear intended passage is not proof that all unintended paths are sealed.

troubleshooting.title: Do not reproduce the study on a pressurized rail
troubleshooting.text: This is a geometric explanation, not a fuel-system service procedure. The model does not simulate pressure relief, fuel discharge, leakage or tool attachment.
